_readme: Narration script. One entry per segment of the Full cut.
Rule: the narration must NOT read the on-screen caption aloud. Captions
carry the specifics; the voice carries the story between them. Hearing a
sentence you are simultaneously reading is the fastest way to make a demo
This rule is easy to write and easy to break — the first draft broke it in
half the beats, because the obvious thing to say about a shot is the thing
already written on it. Before changing a line, open src/beats.ts and read
the caption it plays under. If the two sentences share a phrase, one of
Second rule, learned from the voice itself: no unusual compound words.
Aura-2 read "self-hostable" with the stress of "hostage". It has no SSML
and no phoneme tags, so the fix is different words, not clever spelling —
"it runs on your own servers". Check with: node scripts/voice-check.mjs
open: Running a conference is six spreadsheets, four hundred emails, and a forty thousand dollar tool the customer called slow. Twice. On camera. So here is the same job, start to finish, in one product.
act-Import: It starts the way it always starts. Somebody hands you a spreadsheet.
beat-d-import-2-plan: Don't clean it up first. Drop it in as-is, and watch what comes back.
beat-d-import-record: And if it guessed wrong about a row, you fix that one row — not the whole file.
beat-03-cfp-builder: You build the form yourself, in the app, in an afternoon.
beat-d-cfp-conditional: And it can ask a workshop something it would never ask a lightning talk.
beat-06-public-cfp: Because the best talk you'll get this year is one that someone almost didn't finish submitting.
beat-19-reviewer-scoring: Every committee promises blind review. This one can't cheat.
beat-d-scorecard: So when two reviewers disagree, you can see by how much.
act-Decide: Which makes the decision the easy part.
beat-16-proposals-table: Nobody hears yes before everybody's decided. When you release, it all goes at once.
beat-12-comms: You didn't write any of these.
beat-12b-comms-log: And when a speaker says they never got it, you don't have to guess.
beat-40-gmail-invite: This is not our app. That is a real inbox, and Google has already understood the invitation and offered to put it on her calendar.
beat-agenda-drag: Drag a session wherever you want it. If it can't live there, it says so on the spot. No save, no refresh.
beat-agenda-views: And the same program reads five different ways, because the committee, the attendees and you are not looking for the same thing.
act-Prep: Now the part that usually eats your month.
beat-08-speaker-portal: Give the speakers somewhere to look, and they stop looking at you.
beat-d-speaker-slot: Half your inbox used to be this one question. Now it answers itself.
beat-d-ops-warning: You didn't tell it that someone's headshot was missing. It noticed.
beat-26-speaker-tasks: And the chasing? You never do it again.
beat-realtime: That is why it is built the way it is. You find out at the same moment they do, without asking, and without looking.
act-Publish: And then — the part nobody believes — you're done.
beat-28-public-event-page: One click. No export, no designer, no version that's three weeks stale.
beat-29-embed-widget: And if you already have a website, the program lives there too.
close: That was the job the forty thousand dollar tool was doing. StageStack. It's open source, it runs on your own servers, and it never charges you per event.
